title: No source publishes a claim-side changed-window read for the DP04 build: the operation, its path, its page parameters, its maximum size, its error mapping and a count read all have no source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 sections 12 (published interfaces used: GuaranteeClaimQuery.changedBetween and the note that it returns an empty list until Epic 4), 4, 5 X3, 11 and 13; FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 A2.1 to A2.8; TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.3 and Appendix T-A.1 (two claim operations, neither a read); _work/msr/context/S3.md ownership rows (2 REST operations provided, 0 events, 0 jobs, 1 workflow); RWB-P1-E2010-APP sections 3, 12.2 and 18, which name 'the guarantee claim read of the rwb-guarantee contract' as a contract outside its own Work Package C list (CG-B-P1-02-E2010-101); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and DP-13, R7.2 s12
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 1 to 7; 5 Exception paths X1 to X7; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 8 Business rules BR6 and BR8; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.8; 13 Solution plan Components, Configuration and Build steps; 16 Test cases; 19 Out of scope
description: One combined row for the application slice. (1) The legacy stage 2 step read the claims it needed through an in-process Java call, GuaranteeClaimQuery.changedBetween(from, to), and no source names a consumer-facing REST operation for the claims changed in a business-date window, nor its path, its parameters, its page shape or its maximum page size. (2) The legacy call had no page at all, so paging, its total and the stability of a scan across pages are stated by no source. (3) No source maps an error status to a message for this read: the legacy story gives MSG-GEN-006 for an unavailable interface and the TSD gives 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 for the two published operations, with no message identifier per code. (4) No source gives the claim side of DP04 a count read, although the treatment side has TreatmentQuery.countActive(): the read is therefore written without one and the zero-tolerance count check of BR4 of the legacy story stays on the treatment side. (5) The two operations of TSD S3 T-A.1 are the claim create and the claim update, so the read this story needs is an addition to the published surface of the service that the ownership rows do not carry, while RWB-P1-E2010-APP already names the guarantee claim read as a consumed contract outside its own C list.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 12 'Published interfaces used': 'public interface GuaranteeClaimQuery { List<GuaranteeClaimView> changedBetween(OffsetDateTime from, OffsetDateTime to); }' with the comment 'Guarantee module (S3); returns an empty list until Epic 4'; TSD S3 v2 T-A.1 lists API-S3-001 POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims and API-S3-002 PATCH /api/recovery/v1/guarantee-claims/{claimId} only; _work/msr/context/S3.md gives 2 REST operations provided and 0 events; RWB-P1-E2010-APP section 12.2 lists 'the guarantee claim read of the rwb-guarantee contract' as faked and outside the Work Package's C list.
proposed: Publish one read on the owner of the claim record: GET /api/recovery/guarantee/v1/guarantee-claims?changedFrom=&changedTo=&page=&size=, answering the items, the window, page, size and a scope-filtered total, ordered by updated_at and id, with a declared maximum size and 400 on an empty or inverted window; declare it in the service OpenAPI document and in RWB-P1-E2010-CON as the claim page the DP04 build consumes, with a fake that answers an empty list and an error, and add a count read only if a later release adds a claim-side reconciliation.

title: The owner and the timing of the dated DP04 copy of a guarantee claim conflict: the legacy story writes dp_guarantee_claim itself and puts the claim interface in Epic 4, the target gives the copy to rwb-source-data in wave 2 and the claim record to rwb-guarantee in wave 3
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 sections 2, 11 (DF-TRT-034 to DF-TRT-061 and DF-OPS-001 to DF-OPS-009, all Write), 12 (output dp_guarantee_claim), 13 (Database and build step 1) and section 3 (precondition: the guarantee module publishes GuaranteeClaimQuery, and before it is built in Epic 4 the interface returns no claims); _work/msr/context/S3.md (S3 wave 3, table guarantee_claim, 0 events); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-05, R5.6 W-MAP (EP02 to wave 2) and R4 (S3 wave 3); RWB-P1-E2010-APP sections 2, 12.7 and 19 (dp_guarantee_claim in rwb_source_data, owned by P1)
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 8 and 10; 8 Business rules BR1 and BR6; 11 Data; 12.7; 18 Traceability; 19 Out of scope
description: One combined row for the two disagreements of this legacy key. (1) Owner of the copy: the legacy story writes dp_treatment and dp_guarantee_claim itself, in the single recovery schema; in the target the dated DP04 copies are rwb_source_data's and are built by Stage2ProductWorkflow, while the live claim record is rwb-guarantee's in rwb_guarantee, so this story can only serve the live facts and can neither read nor write dp_guarantee_claim. (2) Timing: this story is EP02 and carries wave 2 by the W-MAP, the rwb-guarantee service is wave 3 in Architecture v5, and the claim record this read serves is first built by the claim stories of the service in EP04; the legacy story's own precondition says the interface returns no claims until Epic 4, so the DP04 build of wave 2 runs against an empty or faked answer and dp_guarantee_claim stays empty until S3 is built.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 3: 'The guarantee module publishes GuaranteeClaimQuery; before it is built (Epic 4), the interface returns no claims'; section 11 marks DF-TRT-034 to DF-TRT-061 and DF-OPS-001 to DF-OPS-009 Write; section 12 'Output: dp_treatment and dp_guarantee_claim rows for D'; RWB-P1-E2010-APP section 12.7 creates dp_guarantee_claim in rwb_source_data; _work/msr/context/S3.md gives S3 wave 3 with table guarantee_claim and 0 events.
proposed: Keep the copy with rwb-source-data in rwb_source_data and the live claim with rwb-guarantee in rwb_guarantee; let RWB-P1-E2010-APP build against the published fake of this read, which answers an empty list until the claim stories of wave 3 land, and let the DP04 guarantee part stay empty rather than stale in wave 2; record the wave difference as a dependency of the DP04 release note, not as a new story.

title: No source says which side resolves a claim whose case does not exist, or whether the claim read answers such a claim at all
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 5 X2, section 7 AC4, section 8 BR3 and section 10 (the recovery service identity writes the breaks); FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 A2.1 to A2.8 (no reference to a case-link check); TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T3.3 (guarantee_claim to recovery_case, many to 1); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-11
section: 4 Flow steps 7 and 8; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC5; 8 Business rules BR6; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.5; 18 Traceability
description: One combined row for the case link. The legacy story holds on the data quality break list any snapshot row whose case does not resolve (check References) and names AC4 as its test, but in the target the case is rwb-case's and is not reachable from this service except by adding a consumed case operation that the Work Package does not list; the functional and technical specifications of S3 name no case-link check at all, and the claim table's many-to-one relationship to recovery_case is a schema statement with no rule attached. So no source says whether this read must refuse a claim whose case does not resolve, flag it, or answer it with its case_id and leave the check to the consumer.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-010 AC4 ('the system does not write the claim to dp_guarantee_claim; the data quality break list holds it with product DP04 and check References') and BR3 ('Every snapshot row links to an existing case, or it is held on the break list'); TSD S3 v2 T3.3 gives the cardinality only; FSD S3 v3 A2.1 to A2.8 carry no case-link rule.
proposed: Answer every claim in the window with its case_id and resolve nothing here: the References check, the break list and the retry stay with RWB-P1-E2010-APP, which already owns the case-existence answer of the DP04 build; if the data steward wants the check pushed to the owner, one case-existence read is added to this service as a consumed contract with a C dependency.
